t.E526.agn: In 1965, JECFA set the ADI for calcium hydroxide as 'not limited'; the evaluation stated that no toxicological reason was seen to limit use in line with good manufacturing practice, but that the total calcium intake from these additives should be kept in mind from a nutritional point of view. In the EU it is a Group I additive; EFSA's re-evaluation has not yet been published (it was included in a call for data in 2016).
t.E526.body: Like calcium in food, the calcium it contains is absorbed in the intestine; in adults about 25% is absorbed, and absorption is regulated by vitamin D. Unabsorbed calcium is excreted in the faeces; the kidneys reabsorb about 98% of the filtered calcium.
t.E526.found.0: May be used at quantum satis (as much as needed) in many foods in the EU
t.E526.found.1: Processed cereal-based foods and baby foods for infants (in the EU only for pH adjustment)
t.E526.prod: It is obtained by burning (calcining) limestone or magnesium minerals.
t.E526.regx.1: Group I additive; generally permitted at quantum satis (as much as needed).
t.E526.regx.2: Included in the call for use/concentration data as part of the re-evaluation (deadline 31.01.2017).
t.E526.regx.3: Permitted only for pH adjustment in processed cereal-based foods and baby foods for infants.
t.E526.summary: Calcium hydroxide (slaked lime). Used in processing maize flour and as an acidity regulator.
t.E526.what: It is a base (slaked lime) used to regulate acidity, to neutralise and to firm texture. In food it reacts with acids to form calcium salts.
